extracted.intended_audience: Goodreads community — readers/reviewers, advance copy readers, authors, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Platform-specific guidelines for leaving ratings and reviews on Goodreads, with a focus on pre-publication (advance copy) feedback and moderation of off-topic reviews. Covers verification, disclosure, shelf-status rules, labeling, and reporting/moderation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading Confirmation for pre-publication ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: A verification process that requires reviewers to confirm they've read the book before rating pre-publication titles. This covers all reading experiences, including readers who didn't finish (DNF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers of pre-publication (advance copy) books must explicitly confirm they have read the book prior to providing a rating; the confirmation applies even if the reviewer did not finish the book. This is intended to improve authenticity of early ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book source transparency for advance copy reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance copy readers are asked to indicate how they obtained their copy (for example, from the publisher or author, Goodreads Giveaways, or other sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosed source will soon appear alongside reviews to help readers understand access context and evaluate potential bias or incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shelf-status requirement for rating (reader-only ratings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers who mark a book as Want to Read cannot rate it until they change their shelf status to Read or Currently Reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule prevents ratings from users who have only expressed interest (Want to Read) and not actually read the book, protecting rating authenticity while preserving the ability to express excitement via shelving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication-status labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the 'Not Yet Published' label to make it clear when a book is forthcoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling forthcoming books helps set appropriate expectations for readers encountering pre-publication listings, reviews, and ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance/focus requirement for reviews (Off-Topic Reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be focused on the book's content, writing, and storytelling; reviews reported for being off-topic will be evaluated against the Rating and Review Guidelines and may not be displayed in the Community Reviews section if they don't comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a review is reported, Goodreads evaluates it for compliance with their Rating and Review Guidelines. Reviews deemed not relevant to the book (e.g., off-topic commentary) can be removed from the Community Reviews area so readers see evaluations that help them judge the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-driven reporting and moderation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone in the Goodreads community can report a review for evaluation; authors and publishers are welcome to report as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you encounter content that may violate the Rating and Review Guidelines, do not engage or respond to it publicly; instead use the report function so Goodreads can assess it. Previously posted content will be reviewed if reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance goal: preserve advance reader insights while improving trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy changes aim to preserve valuable advance reader insights that drive discoverability while supporting readers to see reviews that help them evaluate books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines are designed to maintain the benefits of early feedback for discoverability (e.g., advance reader reviews) while adding verification and transparency measures so reviews and ratings are more trustworthy and useful for other readers.
